Y1.text: Recognise and say numbers up to 10, count aloud to 20 and count objects within 10.
Subitise up to 5 (say how many without counting).
Compare amounts using more, less and equal (the same).
Count in ones, starting from any number.
Place numbers to 20 on a number line and compare them.
Know number facts up to 5.
Become fluent in addition and subtraction facts WITHIN 10.
Count forwards in 2s, 5s and 10s (up to 10 steps, from any multiple), and count in odd numbers.
Recall double facts within 10.
Recall some number bonds to 10.
Know odd and even numbers to 10.
Make numbers TO 10 from 2 parts and split them into parts.
Read, write and explain number sentences using +, − and =, and link them to real-life situations.
Recall all number bond facts FOR 10
Recognise common 2D and 3D shapes in any orientation, and know that shapes with the same name can look different.
Make 2D and 3D shapes from smaller shapes to match an example, turning pieces to fit.
Count to and across 100, forwards and backwards, from any number.
Read and write numbers to 100 in numerals, and numbers 1 to 20 in words.
Find one more and one less than a number.
Use the language equal to, more than, less than, most and least.
Solve one-step multiplication and division problems using objects, pictures and arrays.
Recognise, find and name a half and a quarter of an object, shape or quantity.
Compare and describe lengths, heights, mass, capacity and volume (longer, heavier, full, half full).
Measure and record lengths, mass and capacity using non-standard and simple standard units.
Recognise and know the value of different coins and notes.
Order events in time (before, after, first, today, tomorrow, morning, evening).
Know the days of the week, the months and the language of dates.
Tell the time to the hour and half past the hour, and draw the hands on a clock.
Describe position, direction and movement, including whole, half, quarter and three-quarter turns.

Y2.text: Recognise the place value of each digit in two-digit numbers, and compose and decompose two-digit numbers using standard and non-standard partitioning.
Be secure and fluent in addition and subtraction facts within 10.
Add and subtract across 10.
Understand subtraction as finding the difference, and answer "How many more…?" questions.
Add or subtract ones, or tens, to or from a 2-digit number using known facts.
Add and subtract any two 2-digit numbers using known facts.
Use a written method to add two 2-digit numbers.
Use a written method to subtract one 2-digit number from another.
Write repeated addition as multiplication and find the answer, using the 2, 5 and 10 times tables.
Solve "How many groups?" problems using a missing-number multiplication or a division (grouping).
Recognise fractions as equal parts of a whole shape or a set of objects.
Describe the properties of 2D and 3D shapes using precise vocabulary, and compare shapes by their properties.
Count in steps of 2, 3 and 5 from 0, and in tens from any number.
Read and write numbers to 100 in numerals and words.
Compare and order numbers from 0 to 100 using <, > and =.
Add three one-digit numbers.
Know addition can be done in any order but subtraction cannot, and use the inverse to check answers.
Recognise odd and even numbers.
Write and work out multiplication and division sentences using ×, ÷ and =, and know multiplication can be done in any order.
Find and write 1/3, 1/4, 2/4 and 3/4 of a length, shape, set of objects or quantity.
Know that 2/4 is equivalent to 1/2.
Choose and use standard units to measure length (m, cm), mass (kg, g), temperature (°C) and capacity (l, ml), reading scales to the nearest unit.
Compare and order lengths, mass and capacity using >, < and =.
Use the £ and p symbols, and combine coins to make a given amount.
Solve simple money problems, including giving change.
Tell and write the time to five minutes, including quarter past and quarter to, and draw the hands on a clock.
Know the number of minutes in an hour and hours in a day, and compare and order intervals of time.
Read and make simple pictograms, tally charts, block diagrams and tables.
Answer questions by counting, totalling and comparing the data in each category.
Identify 2D shapes on the faces of 3D shapes.
Describe position and movement, including turns clockwise and anticlockwise and right angles as quarter turns.
Make and continue patterns and sequences of shapes and objects.

Y3.text: Know 10 tens = 1 hundred (100 is 10 times 10), and use it to find how many tens are in multiples of 10 up to 990.
Recognise the place value of each digit in three-digit numbers, and compose and decompose three-digit numbers using standard and non-standard partitioning.
Place any 3-digit number on a number line, and name the multiples of 10 and 100 either side of it.
Split 100 into 2, 4, 5 or 10 equal parts, and read scales marked in these steps (50s, 25s, 20s, 10s).
Be fluent in addition and subtraction facts that cross 10.
Recall the 2, 4, 5, 8 and 10 times tables and their division facts, and recognise multiples of these numbers.
Use known facts to work out facts 10 times bigger.
Recall the 2, 5 and 10 times tables and their division facts, and recognise multiples of these numbers.
Count in multiples of 3 and 6.
Find complements to 100.
Add and subtract up to three-digit numbers using column methods.
Understand addition and subtraction as inverses using part–whole models, and know addition can be done in any order but subtraction cannot.
Apply known multiplication and division facts to solve problems in context, including sharing and grouping.
Read and write proper fractions for parts of a whole split into equal parts.
Find unit fractions of amounts using division facts.
Place any fraction between 0 and 1 on a number line.
Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator, within 1.
Recognise right angles in shapes (in any orientation) and as a quarter turn.
Draw polygons by joining marked points, and identify parallel and perpendicular sides.
Count from 0 in multiples of 50 and 100, and find 10 or 100 more or less than a number.
Compare and order numbers up to 1,000.
Multiply a 2-digit number by a 1-digit number, mentally and using a written method.
Count up and down in tenths, and know tenths come from dividing by 10.
Recognise and show equivalent fractions with small denominators.
Compare and order unit fractions, and fractions with the same denominator.
Measure, compare, add and subtract lengths (m, cm, mm), mass (kg, g) and capacity (l, ml).
Measure the perimeter of simple 2D shapes.
Add and subtract amounts of money and give change, using £ and p.
Tell and write the time from an analogue clock (including Roman numerals I to XII) and 12-hour and 24-hour clocks.
Read time to the nearest minute, use am and pm, and record and compare times in seconds, minutes and hours.
Know the number of seconds in a minute and the number of days in each month, year and leap year.
Read and present data in bar charts, pictograms and tables.
Answer one-step and two-step questions using scaled bar charts, pictograms and tables.
Recognise 3D shapes in different orientations, and describe them.
Identify whether angles are greater or less than a right angle, and identify horizontal and vertical lines.

Y4.text: Know 10 hundreds = 1 thousand (1,000 is 10 times 100), and use it to find how many hundreds are in multiples of 100.
Know the value of each digit in a 4-digit number, and partition it in standard and non-standard ways.
Place any 4-digit number on a number line, name the multiples of 100 and 1,000 either side, and round to the nearest 100 and 1,000.
Split 1,000 into 2, 4, 5 or 10 equal parts, and read scales marked in these steps (500s, 250s, 200s, 100s).
Recall all multiplication and division facts up to 12 × 12, and recognise multiples.
Use known facts to work out facts 100 times bigger.
Know the 11 and 12 times tables.
Know the 3 and 6 times tables.
Know the 7 and 9 times tables.
Divide 2-digit numbers by 1-digit numbers with remainders, and decide what the remainder means in context (round up, round down or ignore).
Multiply and divide whole numbers by 10 and 100 (whole-number answers only), understanding this as making them 10 or 100 times the size.
Rearrange multiplication and division number sentences, and know multiplication can be done in any order.
Use the distributive law to multiply (e.g. 6 × 14 = 6 × 10 + 6 × 4).
Place mixed numbers on a number line and reason about where they sit.
Convert between mixed numbers and improper fractions.
Add and subtract mixed numbers and improper fractions with the same denominator, including crossing whole numbers.
Plot polygons from coordinates in the first quadrant, and translate them.
Know the properties of polygons, including that regular polygons have equal sides and equal angles
Find lines of symmetry in 2D shapes in any orientation, reflect shapes in a line, and complete symmetric figures.
Calculate the perimeter of regular and irregular polygons.
Count in multiples of 6, 7, 9, 25 and 1,000, and find 1,000 more or less than a number.
Count backwards through zero to include negative numbers.
Compare and order numbers beyond 1,000, and round to the nearest 10, 100 or 1,000.
Read Roman numerals to 100 (I to C).
Add and subtract numbers with up to 4 digits using column methods.
Estimate, and use the inverse to check answers.
Multiply 2-digit and 3-digit numbers by a 1-digit number using the formal written method.
Multiply three numbers together, and recognise factor pairs.
Solve scaling and correspondence problems (e.g. 3 hats and 4 coats make 12 outfits).
Recognise families of equivalent fractions.
Count in hundredths, and know hundredths come from dividing by 100.
Know the decimal equivalents of tenths, hundredths, 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4.
Divide 1-digit and 2-digit numbers by 10 and 100, giving tenths and hundredths.
Round decimals with 1 decimal place to the nearest whole number, and compare numbers with up to 2 decimal places.
Find fractions of amounts, including non-unit fractions.
Convert between units of measure (e.g. km and m, kg and g, l and ml).
Find the area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares.
Estimate, compare and calculate with money in £ and p, including decimals.
Read, write and convert between analogue and digital 12-hour and 24-hour clocks.
Convert between units of time (hours and minutes, minutes and seconds, years and months, weeks and days).
Read and present data in bar charts and time graphs.
Solve comparison, sum and difference problems using bar charts, tables and time graphs.
Compare and classify shapes, including types of quadrilateral and triangle.
Identify acute and obtuse angles, and order angles up to two right angles.

Y5.text: Know 10 tenths = 1, 100 hundredths = 1 and 10 hundredths = 1 tenth, and that each place is 10 times the size of the one to its right.
Know the value of each digit in numbers with up to 2 decimal places, and partition them in standard and non-standard ways.
Place any number with up to 2 decimal places on a number line, name the whole numbers and tenths either side, and round to the nearest whole and tenth.
Split 1 into 2, 4, 5 or 10 equal parts, and read scales marked in these steps (0.5, 0.25, 0.2, 0.1).
Use all multiplication facts fluently in multiplication, division and fraction calculations.
Use known facts to work out facts with tenths and hundredths.
Multiply and divide numbers by 10 and 100, including where the answer is a decimal.
Find factors, multiples and prime numbers.
Multiply numbers up to 4 digits by a 1-digit number using short multiplication.
Divide numbers up to 4 digits by a 1-digit number using short division, and decide what the remainder means in context.
Multiply a 4-digit number by a 2-digit number using long multiplication.
Find non-unit fractions of amounts.
Find equivalent fractions, knowing they are equal and represent the same amount
Recall decimal equivalents of halves, quarters, fifths and tenths.
Add and subtract fractions with different denominators.
Add mixed numbers.
Subtract mixed numbers.
Compare and estimate angles in degrees
Compare areas, and calculate the area of rectangles, squares and composite rectilinear shapes in square units.
Measure and draw angles in degrees.
Convert between units of measure, including with simple decimals and fractions.
Read, write, order and compare numbers up to 1,000,000, and count in powers of 10.
Use negative numbers in context, and count forwards and backwards through zero.
Round any number up to 1,000,000 to the nearest 10, 100, 1,000, 10,000 or 100,000.
Read Roman numerals to 1,000 (M), including years.
Add and subtract whole numbers with more than 4 digits, using column methods and mentally.
Use rounding to estimate and check answers, and solve multi-step problems.
Know square and cube numbers and the notation for them (² and ³).
Know prime numbers up to 19, prime factors and composite numbers.
Solve problems involving scaling by simple fractions and simple rates.
Compare and order fractions whose denominators are multiples of the same number.
Multiply proper fractions and mixed numbers by whole numbers.
Read and write decimals as fractions, including thousandths.
Read, write, order, compare and round numbers with up to 3 decimal places.
Know what per cent means, and write percentages as fractions out of 100 and as decimals.
Solve problems using 1/2, 1/4, 1/5, 2/5, 4/5 and fractions with denominators of 10 or 25 as percentages.
Know approximate equivalents between metric units and inches, pounds and pints.
Find the perimeter of composite rectilinear shapes in cm and m.
Estimate volume and capacity.
Solve money problems with all four operations, using decimal notation and scaling.
Solve problems converting between units of time.
Solve comparison, sum and difference problems using a line graph.
Complete, read and interpret tables, including timetables.
Identify 3D shapes, including cubes and cuboids, from 2D drawings.
Know angles at a point add to 360°, angles on a straight line add to 180°, and other multiples of 90°.
Use the properties of rectangles to find missing lengths and angles.
Tell regular and irregular polygons apart by reasoning about sides and angles.
Describe the position of a shape after a reflection or translation.

Y6.text: Understand the relationship between powers of 10 from 1 hundredth to 10 million
Know the value of each digit in numbers up to 10 million, and in decimals, and partition them in standard and non-standard ways.
Place any number up to 10 million, including decimals, on a number line, and round numbers, including in context.
Split any power of 10 (0.01 to 10 million) into 2, 4, 5 or 10 equal parts, and read scales divided in these steps.
Use place value to make a given number 10, 100, 1,000, 1 tenth, 1 hundredth or 1 thousandth times the size (multiply and divide by 10, 100 and 1,000).
Describe how 2 numbers are related by addition (e.g. 4 more) or by multiplication (e.g. 3 times as many).
Use a known calculation to work out related ones (e.g. 24 × 3 = 72, so 24 × 30 = 720).
Multiply a 4-digit number by a 2-digit number using compact column multiplication.
Divide a 3, 4 or 5-digit number by a 2-digit number using long division.
Recognise when fractions can be simplified, and use common factors to simplify fractions.
Write fractions with a common denominator to compare fractions that are close in value.
Compare fractions with different denominators (including above 1) by reasoning, and choose when to use a common denominator instead.
Find common denominators to calculate with fractions.
Find percentages of amounts.
Compare fractions, decimals and percentages.
Solve problems involving ratio relationships.
Solve problems with 2 unknowns.
Draw, make and split shapes from given properties (lengths, angles, area), and solve related problems.
Reflect and translate shapes.
Tell the time and solve time problems.
Use negative numbers in context, and calculate intervals across zero.
Divide numbers up to 4 digits by a 2-digit number using short division where appropriate.
Use the order of operations, and estimate to check answers.
Find common factors, common multiples and prime numbers.
Multiply simple proper fractions, and divide proper fractions by whole numbers.
Convert a fraction to a decimal, and multiply and divide decimals by whole numbers.
Solve problems with missing values using multiplication and division facts.
Solve problems with similar shapes where the scale factor is known or can be found.
Solve problems involving unequal sharing and grouping.
Use simple formulae, and generate and describe linear number sequences.
Express missing-number problems algebraically.
List all the possibilities for combinations of two variables.
Use, read, write and convert units of measure with up to 3 decimal places, and convert between miles and km.
Recognise that shapes with the same area can have different perimeters, and vice versa.
Find the area of parallelograms and triangles.
Find the volume of cubes and cuboids (cm³, m³).
Recognise, describe and build 3D shapes, including making nets.
Find unknown angles in triangles, quadrilaterals and regular polygons, and vertically opposite angles.
Name parts of a circle (radius, diameter, circumference), and know the diameter is twice the radius.
Describe positions on the full coordinate grid (all four quadrants).
Read and make pie charts and line graphs, and use them to solve problems.
Calculate and interpret the mean as an average.
